issues.body: npm_test_targets() scans all of `rest` for `--workspaces`, `-ws`, and workspace selectors without stopping at npm's standalone `--` delimiter. Thus `npm test -- --workspaces` returns ALL_WORKSPACES even though that token is a test-script argument and npm runs only the test selected by the effective working directory. Likewise, `npm run test -- --workspace packages/x` can falsely credit packages/x. This is the same fail-open major issue recorded in round 3, and the test diff still does not exercise either negative case.
issues.fix_hint: Parse npm options only before the first standalone `--`; after that delimiter, treat every token as a script argument and do not recognize workspace flags. Add negative tests proving `npm test -- --workspaces` targets only the effective working directory and `npm run test -- --workspace packages/x` does not credit packages/x, while retaining positive tests for selectors before the delimiter.
issues.title: npm options after `--` are still misread as workspace coverage

verdict.summary: Round 3's major fail-open finding remains unchanged. npm_test_targets() still scans the full argument list for workspace selectors after npm's standalone `--` delimiter, and the added tests still contain no negative cases for selectors passed as script arguments. Consequently, commands such as `npm test -- --workspaces` can falsely credit every workspace even though npm passes `--workspaces` to the package test script. The guard can therefore report repository-wide test coverage that did not execute. Because the same major correctness issue remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
